facts.statement: Ornithopsis is a genus of sauropod dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous of England and possibly Germany.
facts.quote: Ornithopsis (meaning "bird-likeness") is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of England and possibly Germany.

facts.statement: The only currently valid species is O. hulkei, which is known only from fragmentary remains.
facts.quote: The type species, which is the only species seen as valid today, is O. hulkei, which is only known from fragmentary remains.

facts.statement: Seeley identified the fossils as vertebrae with internal cavities for air sacs, a feature seen in pterosaurs and modern birds.
facts.quote: Seeley properly identified the two fossils as vertebrae, and noted that the features considered by Mantell and Owen to indicate the tympanic cavity was in fact openings in the walls of the vertebral centrum, showing that the bones were invaded by cavities for air sacs as seen in both pterosaurs and modern birds.

facts.statement: John Hulke synonymized the genera Eucamerotus and Chondrosteosaurus with Ornithopsis based on shared unique internal vertebral structures.
facts.quote: Hulke also referred the genus Eucamerotus, named earlier by him in 1870, and the genus Chondrosteosaurus to Ornithopsis as junior synonyms, with other fossils found in the Wealden beds showing that they all shared the unique internal structure of Ornithopsis.

facts.statement: The type vertebra of Ornithopsis possesses unique lateral compression and a ventral ridge, identifying it as a diagnostic titanosauriform.
facts.quote: the type vertebra of Ornithopsis shows unique features in its lateral compression and a ventral ridge, and represents a diagnostic titanosauriform.

facts.statement: A fragmentary dorsal vertebra attributed to Ornithopsis was found in northwestern Germany and dates to the Late Barremian-Early Aptian.
facts.quote: In 2023, a fragmentary dorsal vertebra from the Balve in northwestern Germany, preserved in limestone dating to the Late Barremian-Early Aptian, was described.

facts.statement: The referral of the German specimen to Ornithopsis is considered tentative due to poor preservation.
facts.quote: However, the poor preservation of the specimen makes the referral tentative.

facts.statement: In 1882, Richard Lydekker Hulke described the pelvis material NHMUK PV R 97 from the Wealden deposits as a new species named Ornithopsis eucamerotus.
facts.quote: Hulke described pelvis material, NHMUK PV R 97, from the Wealden in 1882

facts.statement: In 1887, Hulke described additional material including vertebrae, ribs, and a pelvis collected by Alfred Nicholson Leeds from the Eyesbury Jurassic deposits of Northamptonshire as the new species Ornithopsis leedsii.
facts.quote: Hulke described more material as Ornithopsis in 1887, for some vertebrae, ribs, a pelvis, and fragments collected in the Eyesbury Jurassic deposits of Northamptonshire by Alfred Nicholson Leeds.

facts.statement: The specimens identified as Ornithopsis leedsii were collected in May 1892 and are stored under catalog numbers NHMUK PV R 1985-1988.
facts.quote: The specimens named as Ornithopsis leedsii are stored as specimens NHMUK PV R 1985-1988, having been collected in May of 1892

facts.statement: In 1874, Hulke named the humerus specimen Ischyrosaurus, suggesting a close relationship to Cetiosaurus oxoniensis and other related genera.
facts.quote: He then gave it the name Ischyrosaurus in 1874

facts.statement: In 1888, Harry Govier Seeley reassigned Cetiosaurus oxoniensis to the genus Ornithopsis as O. oxoniensis, a proposal not immediately endorsed by Lydekker.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus oxoniensis was reassigned to Ornithopsis as O. oxoniensis in 1888 by Harry Govier Seeley

facts.statement: In 1921, Friedrich von Huene described the species Ornithopsis (?) greppini based on a long-tailed cetiosaurid found in Jurassic deposits near Bern, Switzerland.
facts.quote: Huene also described the species Ornithopsis (?) greppini in the same study in 1921, for a long-tailed cetiosaurid from Jurassic deposits around Bern, Switzerland.

facts.statement: In 2020, the species formerly known as Ornithopsis greppini was assigned to the new genus Amanzia following a redescription of the original material.
facts.quote: Ornithopsis greppini was given the new genus name Amanzia in a 2020 redescription of the original material.

facts.statement: In a 2004 review of sauropods, Upchurch et al. listed Ornithopsis manseli as a dubious sauropod.
facts.quote: Upchurch et al., in their review of sauropods (2004), listed it as a dubious sauropod.

facts.statement: The holotype of Ornithopsis hulkei consists of a single vertebra centrum that lacks a neural spine.
facts.quote: The Ornithopsis hulkei holotype is basically a centrum lacking the neural spine.

facts.statement: The holotype vertebra is heavily pneumatized, containing large internal cavities known as camellae.
facts.quote: The vertebra is heavily pneumatised, filled with large cavities, camellae.

facts.statement: The holotype vertebra is narrow and tall, features a ridge on its underside, is opisthocoelous, and possesses a deep subtriangular pleurocoel located posteriorly over two-thirds of its length.
facts.quote: It is narrow, tall, has a ridge on the underside, is opisthocoelous and has a posteriorly placed deep subtriangular pleurocoel over two thirds of its length.

facts.statement: Comparisons with Giraffatitan estimate the holotype specimen of Ornithopsis hulkei to be between 16 and 18 meters in length.
facts.quote: Based on comparison with Giraffatitan, the holotype specimen is estimated to be 16-18 m in length

facts.statement: In an early 1927 review, Friedrich von Huene retained Ornithopsis greppini in the genus, considering it part of a group containing O. hulkei, O. leedsii, O. humerocristatus, O. manseli, and O. (?) greppini.
facts.quote: Huene retained O. greppini in the genus in an early 1927 review of sauropods, considering the genus to contain the species Ornithopsis hulkei, O. leedsii, O. humerocristatus, O. manseli, and O. (?) greppini

facts.statement: Cetiosaurus leedsi was later assigned to an intermediate member of Brachiosauridae, with debate over whether it was a proper species of Ornithopsis or an indeterminate eusauropod.
facts.quote: Cetiosaurus leedsi was then assigned to an intermediate member of Brachiosauridae, considered to be a proper species of Ornithopsis, or an improper species of Ornithopsis that is an indeterminate eusauropod.

facts.statement: The fossil range of Ornithopsis hulkei is the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico inferior

facts.statement: Ornithopsis hulkei is classified within the unranked family Titanosauriformes.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Titanosauriformes

facts.statement: The genus Ornithopsis was established by Seeley in 1870.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Seeley, 1870

facts.statement: The species O. hulkei was described by Seeley in 1870.
facts.quote: species_authority: Seeley, 1870

facts.statement: Ornithopsis leedsii was distinguished from other Ornithopsis specimens by its much larger size, robusticity, and older age, despite similarities in vertebrae and pelvis structure.
facts.quote: The vertebrae and pelvis showed many similarities with the specimens of Ornithopsis from the Wealden Group, but the much larger size of the Eyesbury specimens, their robusticity, and their older age were considered sufficient to describe as a new species

facts.statement: A 2010 overview noted that Ornithopsis manseli shares features with both Rebbachisauridae and Titanosauriformes but lacks sufficient characteristics to determine its exact phylogenetic position.
facts.quote: A 2010 overview of Late Jurassic sauropods from Dorset noted that O. manseli shared features seen in both Rebbachisauridae and Titanosauriformes, but lacked features to nail down its exact phylogenetic position.

facts.statement: Ornithopsis is a dubious extinct genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur containing only one known species, Ornithopsis hulkei.
facts.quote: Ornithopsis hulkei es la única especie conocida del género dudoso extinto Ornithopsis (gr. "apariencia de ave") de dinosaurio saurópodo titanosauriforme

facts.statement: Ornithopsis hulkei was a large sauropod that reached a length of 24 meters.
facts.quote: Ornithopsis es un saurópodo de gran tamaño, que tenía 24 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The animal possessed a typical brachiosaurid nasal arch, had front legs longer than its hind legs, was herbivorous, and moved on four legs.
facts.quote: Poseía el típico arco nasal de los braquiosáuridos y largas patas delanteras comparadas con las traseras, siendo herbívoro y cuadrúpedo.

facts.statement: The type species Ornithopsis hulkei was named and described by Harry Govier Seeley in 1870.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Ornithopsis hulkei, fue nombrada y descrita por Harry Govier Seeley en 1870.

facts.statement: The type material consisted of two dorsal vertebrae found in East Sussex and on the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: El tipo constaba de dos vértebras dorsales, NHMUK R.2239, que se encontró en el Grupo Hastings de East Sussex y NHMUK R.28632 encontrado en la Isla de Wight en la Formación Wessex

facts.statement: Seeley named the genus Ornithopsis because he considered the animal an intermediate form bridging the gap between pterosaurs, birds, and dinosaurs.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del griego ὄρνις, ornis, "pájaro", en ὄψις, opsis, "cara" o "semejanza", una referencia al hecho de que Seeley consideraba que el animal era una forma intermedia que salvaba la brecha entre los pterosaurios, los pájaros y dinosaurios.

facts.statement: The specific name hulkei honors John Whitaker Hulke.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra a John Whitaker Hulke.

facts.statement: In 1882, John Whitaker Hulke grouped all Ornithopsis and Eucamerotus vertebrae under the new name Ornithopsis eucamerotus along with three pelvic bones.
facts.quote: En 1882, Hulke agrupó todas las vértebras de Ornithopsis y Eucamerotus bajo el nuevo nombre Ornithopsis eucamerotus junto con un conjunto de tres huesos pélvicos

facts.statement: In 1995, William Blows restricted Ornithopsis to specimen NHMUK R.28632, assigning other referred vertebrae to Eucamerotus.
facts.quote: En 1995 William Blows restringió Ornithopsis a NHMUK R.28632, asignando otras vértebras referidas al género a Eucamerotus

facts.statement: In 1887, Hulke named Ornithopsis leedsii based on vertebrae and partial pelvic remains found near Peterborough by Alfred Nicholson Leeds.
facts.quote: En 1887, Hulke nombró Ornithopsis leedsii para NHMUK R1984-1988, vértebras y restos parciales de una pelvis encontrados por Alfred Nicholson Leeds cerca de Peterborough.

facts.statement: Ornithopsis leedsii was later renamed Cetiosaurus leedsi and then Cetiosauriscus leedsii, both now considered incorrect identifications.
facts.quote: Esta especie pasaría a llamarse Cetiosaurus leedsi y más tarde Cetiosauriscus leedsii, ambos considerados hoy como identificaciones incorrectas.

facts.statement: The holotype of Ornithopsis hulkei is basically a centrum lacking a neural spine.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Ornithopsis hulkei es básicamente un centro que carece de la espina neural.

facts.statement: The vertebra is strongly pneumatized and filled with large cavities.
facts.quote: La vértebra está fuertemente neumatizada, llena de grandes cavidades, camelas.

facts.statement: The vertebra is narrow and tall, has a crest on the bottom, is opisthocoelous, and features deep, posteriorly placed subtriangular pleurocoels extending over two-thirds of its length.
facts.quote: Es estrecho, alto, tiene una cresta en la parte inferior, es opistocélica y tiene una profunda posteriormente colocado subtriangulares pleurocoelos más de dos tercios de su longitud.

facts.statement: These characteristics are compatible with a placement within the Titanosauriformes.
facts.quote: Estas características son compatibles con una ubicación dentro de los Titanosauriformes.

facts.statement: Ornithopsis eucamerotus is a nomen dubium synonymized with Chondrosteosaurus gigas.
facts.quote: Ornithopsis eucamerotus Hulke 1882 - nomen dubium sinonimizado con Chondrosteosaurus gigas.

facts.statement: Ornithopsis leedsii is a nomen dubium that is indeterminate beyond Eusauropoda.
facts.quote: Ornithopsis leedsii Hulke 1887 = Cetiosaurus leedsi (Hulke 1887) Woodward 1905 = Cetiosauriscus leedsii (Hulke 1887) von Huene 1927 = nomen dubium; indeterminado más allá de Eusauropoda.

facts.statement: Ornithopsis greppini is synonymized with Amanzia.
facts.quote: Ornithopsis greppini von Huene 1922 = Amanzia

facts.statement: Ornithopsis lived in the early Cretaceous, approximately 130 million years ago during the Barremian stage, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 130 millones de años, en el Barremiense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: The genus Ornithopsis has a recorded time range from the Tithonian to the Aptian (145.06 to 119.57 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Aptian (145.06 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: Ornithopsis belongs to the parent group Titanosauriformes.
facts.quote: Parent group: Titanosauriformes

facts.statement: Ornithopsis is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: The genus name Ornithopsis means "bird-like face" and reflects Seeley's belief that the animal was an intermediate form between pterosaurs, birds, and dinosaurs.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del griego ὄρνις, ornis, "pájaro", en ὄψις, opsis, "cara" o "semejanza", una referencia al hecho de que Seeley consideraba que el animal era una forma intermedia que salvaba la brecha entre los pterosaurios, los pájaros y dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Richard Owen rejected Seeley's creation of the genus Ornithopsis and his evolutionary interpretation of the material.
facts.quote: La creación de Seeley del género, sin embargo, no fue aceptada por Richard Owen, quien rechazó la interpretación evolutiva del material.
